STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE  
REFRIGERATED CARGO HANDLING & COLD CHAIN INTEGRITY  
SOP-LOG-044 | Version 2.1 | Effective Date: April 5, 2024  
Meridian Maritime & Freight | meridianfreight.com  

**Purpose:**  
To ensure the integrity of temperature-sensitive cargo throughout transit by establishing standardized procedures for setpoint verification, continuous monitoring, and immediate response to deviations that threaten product quality or regulatory compliance.

**Scope:**  
Applies to all refrigerated units (reefers) operated by Meridian Maritime & Freight carrying perishable goods, including but not limited to pharmaceuticals, fresh produce, dairy, and frozen seafood.

**Procedure:**

1. **Pre-Trip Inspection (PTI) & Setpoint Verification**  
   Prior to loading, the assigned Equipment Technician shall:  
   - Confirm the reefer unit’s setpoint matches the shipper’s documented requirement (±0.5°C tolerance allowed during setup).  
   - Verify alarm thresholds are configured to trigger at ±1.5°C deviation from setpoint.  
   - Inspect door seals, insulation, airflow channels, and refrigerant levels per PTI Checklist LOG-044-A.  
   - Validate data logger functionality and battery status; ensure logging interval is set to **every 15 minutes**.  
   - Document all findings in the PTI log and obtain sign-off from Operations Lead before release for loading.

2. **Continuous Monitoring During Transit**  
   - Temperature data shall be logged automatically every 15 minutes via integrated telematics system.  
   - Real-time alerts are generated if temperature exceeds ±1.5°C from setpoint for more than 15 consecutive minutes (i.e., two consecutive logged readings outside threshold).  
   - Persistent breach (defined as two or more consecutive out-of-range readings) triggers immediate escalation.

3. **Escalation Protocol**  
   Upon detection of a persistent temperature breach:  
   - The automated system alerts the On-Duty Operations Lead (**Marcus Vance, mvance@meridianfreight.com**) and Chief Engineer (**Eng. Lindholm, klindholm@meridianfreight.com**) via SMS and email within 2 minutes.  
   - Vance and Lindholm shall initiate root cause assessment, contact vessel/terminal ops, and determine corrective actions (e.g., power swap, unit replacement, reroute).  
   - If breach persists beyond 30 minutes from initial alert, Operations Lead shall notify the consignee (e.g., EuroFresh Imports) within **2 hours** of breach confirmation, providing:  
     - Current temperature status and duration of deviation  
     - Estimated time to recovery  
     - Risk assessment and mitigation steps taken  
   - All communications and actions shall be logged in the Incident Response Form LOG-044-B.

4. **Post-Incident Review**  
   All temperature excursions require a post-trip review within 24 hours of discharge to determine root cause and update preventive measures.

**Compliance:**  
Non-compliance with this SOP may result in cargo rejection, financial liability, and disciplinary action. Audits conducted quarterly by Quality Assurance.

**Approved By:**  
Director of Logistics Operations  
Meridian Maritime & Freight  
*Document Control: SOP-LOG-044 | Review Cycle: Annual | Next Review: April 5, 2025*  
---

# Q4 2026 Ocean Freight Rate Schedule & Demurrage Policy  
**Meridian Maritime & Freight**

## Base Container Rates – North Europe to Mediterranean  
Effective October 1, 2026, through December 31, 2026:

| Container Type | Base Rate |
|----------------|-----------|
| 20ft Standard Dry | $1,450 USD |
| 40ft High Cube (HC) | $2,100 USD |

*Base rates apply to door-to-port or port-to-door shipments between designated North Europe hubs (Rotterdam, Antwerp, Hamburg) and Mediterranean ports (Valencia, Barcelona, Genoa, Piraeus). Rates exclude origin/destination handling, customs, and terminal charges.*

## Bunker Adjustment Factor (BAF)  
The BAF is calculated monthly using the **Rotterdam VLSFO (Very Low Sulphur Fuel Oil)** price index as published by Platts. The adjustment is applied as a per-TEU surcharge, updated on the first business day of each month. For Q4 2026, the BAF will be indexed to the average Rotterdam VLSFO price for September, October, and November 2026, respectively. Current BAF estimates range from $180–$220/TEU, subject to market volatility.

## Demurrage & Detention Policy  
- **Free Time:** Exactly **5 standard business days** permitted at the discharge port for container pickup, beginning the day after vessel discharge (gate-in timestamp). Weekends and recognized port holidays are excluded.  
- **After Free Time:**  
  - Dry Containers: **$145 USD per calendar day**  
  - Refrigerated Units (Reefer): **$290 USD per calendar day**  
Charges accrue from the first day beyond free time until empty container return to designated depot (detention) or until pickup from terminal (demurrage), whichever applies.

## Dispute Procedure  
All demurrage/detention disputes must be submitted in writing to **Meridian Port Dispatch** via email at `portdispatch@meridianfreight.com` within **7 calendar days** of the invoice date. Submissions must include:  
- Bill of Lading number  
- Container number(s)  
- Official gate-in and gate-out timestamps (from terminal operator)  
- Supporting documentation (e.g., customs clearance, trucker receipt)  

Claims received after 7 calendar days will not be considered. Meridian Maritime & Freight reserves the right to audit all timestamps and adjust charges accordingly.  

*This schedule supersedes all prior versions. For full terms, refer to Meridian’s Standard Trading Conditions (STC 2026).*

HAZARDOUS MATERIALS & DANGEROUS GOODS COMPLIANCE BULLETIN  
(HAZMAT-2026-09)  
Meridian Maritime & Freight | Issued: September 1, 2026 | Effective Immediately

This bulletin reinforces critical IMDG Code compliance requirements for the safe handling, stowage, and transport of Class 3 Flammable Liquids aboard all Meridian-operated vessels and terminals.

**IMDG Segregation Requirements – Class 3:**  
Class 3 flammable liquids must be segregated from Classes 1 (Explosives), 2.1 (Flammable Gases), 4.1 (Flammable Solids), 5.1 (Oxidizing Substances), and 8 (Corrosives) unless specific exceptions under IMDG 7.2.4 apply. Stowage must prevent dangerous reactions due to leakage, spillage, or mixing. Use approved segregation tables and consult the Cargo Securing Manual for vessel-specific arrangements.

**Minimum Separation Distance:**  
All Class 3 cargo must be stowed a minimum of **3 meters horizontally** and **2 meters vertically** from accommodation areas, machinery spaces, and any permanent or temporary ignition sources (including electrical equipment, open flames, hot work, and smoking areas). Vertical separation applies where direct vertical alignment exists; horizontal separation is required in all other configurations.

**MSDS Pre-Declaration Timeline:**  
A valid, up-to-date Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS/SDS) for each Class 3 substance must be submitted to Meridian’s Dangerous Goods Acceptance Team **no less than 24 hours prior to terminal gate-in**. Failure to comply will result in cargo refusal and potential delays. Electronic submission via the Meridian DG Portal is mandatory.

**Emergency Spill Response:**  
In the event of a leak, spill, or fire involving Class 3 materials, immediately activate the vessel’s SOPEP and contact the 24/7 Meridian Dispatch Desk at **+31-10-555-0199**. Provide vessel name, voyage number, cargo location, and nature of incident.

**Port Authority Reporting – UN1203/UN1993:**  
All shipments of UN1203 (Gasoline) and UN1993 (Flammable Liquid, n.o.s.) are subject to enhanced port authority verification. Ensure correct UN number, proper shipping name, packing group, and emergency contact details are accurately declared on the Dangerous Goods Declaration. Non-compliance may trigger detention, fines, or denial of entry.

Compliance is non-negotiable. Questions? Contact HSE Compliance: hse@meridianmaritime.com or ext. 7742. — End of Bulletin —

# PORT OF ROTTERDAM — BONDED WAREHOUSE (TYPE II) PROCEDURES & TRANSIT CLEARANCE  
*Meridian Maritime & Freight – Maasvlakte Logistics Park*

## Overview  
This document outlines the operational procedures for Type II bonded warehouse facilities operated by Meridian Maritime & Freight at the Maasvlakte Logistics Park, Port of Rotterdam. All activities comply with EU Union Customs Code (UCC) and Dutch Customs Authority (Douane) regulations.

## Key Procedures  

### **Transit Declaration Requirement**  
For all non-EU cleared consignments entering or transiting through the bonded warehouse, a valid **T1 transit declaration** is mandatory under the New Computerised Transit System (NCTS). The T1 must be lodged prior to arrival and remain active until discharge or re-export. Failure to present a valid T1 will result in customs hold and potential penalties.

### **Customs Release Inspection Codes**  
Release from bonded storage is governed by the following inspection codes:  
- **Code 44B**: Standard physical examination of goods (mandatory for high-risk or randomly selected consignments).  
- **Code 12A**: Documentary release only — permitted when risk assessment indicates low concern and all documentation is complete and compliant.  
Inspection code assignment is determined by Dutch Customs via NCTS risk analysis; Meridian staff must not alter or override these codes.

### **Bonded Storage Tariff**  
Storage fees apply after the initial 48-hour transit window (free period).  
- **Rate**: EUR 18.50 per TEU per calendar day.  
- Charges accrue from hour 49 onward and are invoiced monthly.  
- Fractions of a day are rounded up to the next full day.  
- Rates are subject to quarterly review; current tariff effective 1 January 2024.

### **Compliance Oversight**  
All bonded warehouse operations are supervised by:  
**Helena Chen**, Customs Compliance Officer  
Contact: h.chen@meridianfreight.nl | +31 (0)10 123 4567  
Ms. Chen ensures adherence to UCC, NCTS protocols, and Douane audit requirements. Any procedural queries, discrepancies, or audit preparations must be directed to her office.

## General Notes  
- Goods must remain under customs supervision at all times while in bond.  
- No manipulation, processing, or removal of goods is permitted without prior customs authorization.  
- All documentation (T1, CMR, packing lists, commercial invoices) must be retained for minimum 3 years and made available upon request.  
- Violations may result in suspension of bonded status, fines, or criminal liability under Dutch Customs Act.

*Last updated: April 2024 | Version 2.1*  
*Approved by: Helena Chen, Customs Compliance Officer*  
*Meridian Maritime & Freight – Maasvlakte Logistics Park, Rotterdam*
